what_is_this: Condensed log of the founding conversation between Naresh Silla and Claude (Fable 5) that produced BhavBench, 2026-07-19 to 2026-07-20. Tool calls and internal reasoning omitted; each entry preserves the intent of the user's message and the substance of the assistant's response. Future agents: read PLAN.md first (it is the authoritative build spec); this file explains how and why decisions were made in sequence. MAINTENANCE RULE: any agent doing a working session on this project MUST append a turn entry summarizing the user's asks and what shipped, in the same commit as the work.
project: BhavBench — emotional & cultural intelligence benchmark for Indian conversations
repo_state_at_log_end: Final v1 board shipped: 27 rows across 14 labs incl. Claude Fable 5 (#1, 9.47), Kimi K3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5, and Sarvam 30B/105B at low+high reasoning. Site live at https://bhavbench.vercel.app. All history authored as silla.naresh@gmail.com.

turns.user: I want to get into Sarvam AI as a product manager and need one extremely solid portfolio project showing deep product sense plus real understanding of AI/evals. Not a shallow or common idea. My own idea: an eval benchmark for the human-emotions side of models (not coding benchmarks like SWE-bench) — with a UI showing rankings of all top models and infra to run the eval on any model. I lack psychology expertise, so you bring that. Show me a list of ideas first, then we pick.
turns.assistant: Researched first. Found: (a) the raw idea already exists — EQ-Bench 3 (45 multi-turn roleplay scenarios, LLM-judged, Elo, eqbench.com); (b) Sarvam's entire moat is culturally fluent Indic AI (11 languages, 100M+ enterprise conversations, $234M Series B); (c) the open gap: no serious benchmark for whether models understand INDIAN emotional/social dynamics — CuLEmo is 400 single-turn questions, nothing multi-turn, no leaderboard, no code-mixing. Proposed 5 ideas, recommended #1: an emotional & cultural intelligence benchmark for Indian conversations (working name BhavBench) — compete on cultural pragmatics where the user IS the domain expert, not on clinical psychology where EQ-Bench lives. Headline artifact: 'frontier models top English EQ benchmarks but score X on Indian emotional context.'

turns.user: Idea 1 it is. Questions: how do we get the dataset (do I need friends' chat histories?), Sarvam isn't on OpenRouter (I have OpenRouter credits, can buy Sarvam credits). Before building: write an extremely detailed PLAN.md (so future agents can continue), a README.md explaining product sense + psychology/domain knowledge + tech, push to GitHub before coding, then start the dataset.
turns.assistant: Answered: real private chats are the WRONG data source (consent, PII, unpublishable, no dimensional control) — the correct method is original hand-curated scenarios: taxonomy grid, LLM-assisted drafts, human rewrite, anti-stereotype review; the user's curation is itself the interview story. Sarvam: native adapter against api.sarvam.ai planned; weights are open as fallback. Then shipped M0: PLAN.md (8 dimensions with psychology groundings — Hall high-context, Hofstede power distance, Markus & Kitayama, face theory, Gumperz code-switching; matched en/hing/hi language triplets; scripted-user roleplay + transcript-analysis tasks; probe-turn design; judge protocol with bias controls and human-calibration gate; full edge-case policy; page-by-page UI/UX spec; milestones M0-M6; scope fences), README.md (product/domain/tech framing), taxonomy + schema + authoring checklist + anchored rubrics, 6 pilot scenarios with full triplets, dataset validator (6/6 green), canary string. Committed and pushed.

turns.user: Start executing and don't stop until the job is complete — take hours or days, give your best.

turns.user: OK, complete with the models already done. And why show sample data on an end-user UI at all?
turns.assistant: Agreed — sample was scaffolding, now obsolete. Archived all mock runs out of the scoring path. Budget forced a methodology decision: $1.65 could not fund two judges for all 12 models, and MIXING one-judge and two-judge models would bias ranks (Qwen strictly harsher) — so switched to ONE uniform judge (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite) for every model, kept Qwen judgments visible in transcript views tagged 'cross-check only', documented everything on the methodology page.

Drove judging to completion; first full scoring revealed error items (reasoning models starved to empty text at max_tokens=1024; GLM's provider dropping connections). Per the plan's no-silent-errors rule, ran a repair pass (max_tokens→2000), added a coverage rule (models under 40/50 items are EXCLUDED, not misleadingly ranked) and a 'partial N/50' disclosure chip. Credits ran to $0 on the final judgment call.

Final board shipped: 11 real models, 9 labs, ~$4.97 total. MiniMax M3 8.27 (43/50 disclosed) > GPT-5.6 Luna 7.78 > Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite 7.61 > DeepSeek V4 Pro 7.27 > ... > Llama 4 Maverick 3.23. GLM-4.7 excluded (30/50). Findings written into paper §5 from artifacts: support control 7.72 vs cultural dimensions 6.58; weakest = indirectness 5.36, money 5.66; 9/11 models drop en→hi (mean +0.69); DeepSeek V4 Pro's Hindi collapse +3.23; GPT-5.6 Luna slightly BETTER in Hindi (−0.27). Site rebuilt real-only, pushed, PR #1 merged to main.
